subject: Measurement pixel disclosure & DPA: request for transfer matrix and evidence
messages:
From: Julie Choe <julie.choe@acme-marketing.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@acme-marketing.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Measurement pixel — need scope + transfers for DPA

Hi Soojin / Ben,

We're preparing our updated DPA and need to confirm how Redwood handles the small measurement pixel JS that our marketing team deploys via the Console. Specifically we need:

- A short description of what the pixel collects by default (cookies, client IP, user-agent, any identifiers).
- Whether any payload from that pixel is ever treated as PII by Redwood (or used to re-identify users).
- A current list of subprocessors that may process pixel telemetry and the hosting regions for those subprocessors (we're focused on cross-border transfer obligations).
- Any available evidence (SOC2 report summary, architecture/dataflow diagram, or export showing subprocessor locations).

Can you also confirm whether providing the pixel to Redwood implies we need a DPA amendment or if the existing DPA covers this measurement telemetry?

I'm attaching a rough diagram we use on our end for context (pixel_dataflow_v1.png). Our legal/privacy team would like to close this within the week.

Thanks,
Julie
Julie Choe
Privacy Lead — Acme Marketing
privacy@acme-marketing.com

---
Attachment: pixel_dataflow_v1.png (diagram, 240KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Julie Choe <julie.choe@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Measurement pixel — need scope + transfers for DPA

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and we'll follow up with legal and security docs: 

- Default collection: the Console pixel captures client IP, user-agent, timestamp, and an event payload that is customer-controlled. By default we do not append Redwood-level identifiers.
- PII: Redwood does not intentionally enrich or re-identify telemetry. If you send user identifiers in the payload (email, user id) that data will be processed per the DPA as "Customer Content".
- Subprocessors/hosts: we operate Console ingestion in customer-configurable regions; commonly data traverses AWS EU (eu-west-1) and us-east-1 for fallback. We’ll provide a full subprocessor list and regions export.
- DPA amendment: likely an addendum to call out front-end pixel telemetry as a processed data type for marketing analytics; legal can confirm.

Attaching a short Console dataflow summary and a link to our compliance folder. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Julie — adding a couple of practical notes from sales/ops side: 

- In practice most customers run the pixel as "non-identifying telemetry" (events only). If your tag includes user_id/email we recommend redacting before sending to Console or using tokenized ids.
- We'll produce the subprocessor export CSV (last generated 2026-11-16) showing vendor names and country locations — see attached.
- If you need a signed addendum we can route via DocuSign once legal confirms the language.

Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Julie Choe <julie.choe@acme-marketing.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Measurement pixel — need scope + transfers for DPA

Hi Julie — looping in from legal. A few clarifications and requested artifacts so we can assess amendment scope: 

1) Role and legal basis: Redwood is a processor under our DPA. Data sent in pixel payloads is Customer Content where you control the schema. If that payload contains identifiers we will treat it as Customer Content and apply the DPA controls.

2) Subprocessors/transfers: the attached CSV contains our current subprocessor inventory. Key points: ingestion and short-term caching are in EU (eu-west-1) by default; we have optional replication to US (us-east-1) for latency/failover in some Dedicated accounts. Where data leaves EEA we rely on SCCs and our vendor contracts.

3) Evidence: we can provide a SOC2 Type II summary and a redacted network/dataflow diagram. For EU customers concerned about transfers, we typically offer either region-locking (EU-only retention) or an addendum that states region controls plus SCCs.

Next steps we propose:
- You provide a sample pixel telemetry schema (field names, examples) and any retention expectations.
- Redwood will provide: (a) subprocessor+region matrix export, (b) SOC2 summary, (c) proposed DPA addendum language.

If those items work, I can prepare a DocuSign envelope for the addendum and route to your legal team.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
